question: Who Owns Chipotle?
quick_answer: Chipotle is an independent, publicly traded company listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker CMG, so it is owned by its shareholders rather than a parent company. McDonald's was once a major investor and helped Chipotle grow, but it fully sold its stake by 2006. Chipotle was founded in 1993 by Steve Ells in Denver, Colorado.

Known for build-your-own burritos and bowls

body.heading: Who owns Chipotle?
body.text: Chipotle Mexican Grill is a public company, which means it is owned collectively by its shareholders. It trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker CMG and is run by its own management and board, not controlled by a larger restaurant conglomerate.

body.heading: The McDonald's connection
body.text: A common question is whether McDonald's owns Chipotle. McDonald's did invest heavily in Chipotle in its early years and at one point held a large stake, which helped fund Chipotle's expansion. However, McDonald's fully divested its shares by 2006, around the time Chipotle went public, so the two companies are not connected today.

body.heading: The brand's roots
body.text: Chipotle was founded in 1993 by Steve Ells, who opened the first location in Denver, Colorado. It pioneered the fast-casual, build-your-own burrito and bowl model and grew into one of the largest Mexican-style chains in the US as an independent public company.

faqs.a: No. McDonald's was a major early investor but sold its entire stake by 2006. Chipotle is now an independent, publicly traded company.
Yes. Chipotle trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol CMG, so it is owned by its shareholders.
Chipotle was founded in 1993 by Steve Ells in Denver, Colorado.
